from_statement_quote: DRAFT independent obstruction, review pending. Let T_i be iid positive integers with P(T_i=m)=1/[m(m+1)], m>=1. Set S_k=sum_{i=1}^k T_i and Y_t=max{k:S_k<=t}. Then T_i is finite almost surely, P(T_i>=m)=1/m and E[T_i]=infinity. Strong laws for the truncations min(T_i,M), followed by M increasing to infinity, give S_k/k -> infinity. Thus Y_t -> infinity but Y_t/t -> 0 almost surely despite unit regeneration displacements. This holding process is outside uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor iid RWRE and does not refute C0041; it refutes only an inference from finite-a.s. regeneration times and bounded displacements to positive speed.

from_statement_quote: DRAFT sufficient bridge, review pending; combines the independently audited w453 outward-face argument with w454 conditioning. Let X start at 0 in Z^d in a nearest-neighbor environment with every transition at least kappa, 0<kappa<=1/(2d). Let tau be an arbitrary nonnegative integer random time, R_tau the maximum infinity-norm of the path up to tau, and D any event with P(D)=p>0. For integers r,t>=0, P(tau>t|D)<=P(R_tau>r|D)+p^-1(1-kappa^(r+1))^floor(t/(r+1)). The deterministic-time cube survival estimate is proved in the original law by conditional iteration, then divided by p; the conditioned law is not assumed to retain ellipticity. If P(R_tau>r|D)<=C exp(-lambda r) with lambda>log(1/kappa), this bound is summable in t and gives E[tau|D]<infinity. C0041 does not supply that radius-tail rate in this derivation, and the condition is sufficient, not necessary.
